claim.pdf_says: In the interface-definition general format, INTERFACE-ID, AS, INHERITS, USING, END and INTERFACE are underlined (required words) while FROM is NOT underlined: '[ INHERITS FROM { interface-name-2 } … ]' shows an underline under INHERITS only (verified on a 300 dpi crop of the printed line).
claim.markdown_says: The interface-definition figure (lines 12581-12592) is a plain fenced code block with no underline marking and — unlike the adjacent method-definition figure, which carries a '> **Figure notes (method-definition general format).** ... are underlined in the printed standard (required words); `IS` is not underlined.' blockquote — no compensating figure note: '[ INHERITS FROM { interface-name-2 } … ]'
claim.why_it_matters: Underlining is how the standard's meta-language distinguishes required words from optional words. With it dropped and no figure note, the markdown gives no way to tell that FROM in 'INHERITS FROM' is an optional word (so 'INHERITS interface-name-2' is legal) while INHERITS itself is required. The immediately following figure on the same page does carry that note, so the omission is an oversight, not a transcription policy.

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute this three ways and failed on all three.

(1) GLYPH READING — I rendered page 289 at 300 dpi and then magnified the interface-definition figure ~2x beyond that (crops E:/Temp/specrecon/v289/crop_inherits.png and crop_iface_full.png). What I see with my own eyes on the printed line '[ INHERITS FROM { interface-name-2 } … ]' is a rule that starts under the 'I' of INHERITS, runs to the 'S', and STOPS in the inter-word space. There is unambiguously NO rule under F-R-O-M — the gap between the end of the INHERITS underline and the baseline under FROM is white, at a magnification where the individual underlines beneath the shorter words (AS: a ~2-character rule; END: a ~3-character rule) are plainly resolved. So the underline pattern in that figure is: IDENTIFICATION, DIVISION, INTERFACE-ID, AS, INHERITS, USING, END, INTERFACE underlined; FROM not underlined. (The claim's word list omits IDENTIFICATION and DIVISION, which are also underlined — an incomplete list, not a false one.)

(2) IS THE INFORMATION ACTUALLY PRESENT, REFLOWED OR ADJACENT? No. specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 12581-12592 (the exact range the claim cites — fence opens at 12581, closes at 12592) is a bare fenced block with no underline, no bold, no marker of any kind. The only figure-notes blockquote on the page is line 12611, and it is explicitly scoped '(method-definition general format)' and enumerates only METHOD-ID/GET/SET/PROPERTY/OVERRIDE/FINAL/END/METHOD/IS. Nothing anywhere on the page states which words of the interface-definition figure are required.

(3) IS THIS MERE FORMATTING, OR A BLANKET TRANSCRIPTION POLICY THAT DOESN'T CHANGE MEANING? This was the strongest refutation path and it does not hold. Underlining in a COBOL general format is normative meta-language, not typography: the standard's own 5.2.5/5.2.6 text, transcribed at ISO_COBOL.md lines 2628, 2641 and 5805, says keywords 'are shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats' and are 'required', while 'uppercase words that are not underlined are called optional words and may be specified at the user's option with no effect on the semantics of the format.' So the dropped rule under FROM is precisely the difference between 'INHERITS FROM Base' being the only legal spelling and 'INHERITS Base' also being legal. The standard's own examples settle which reading is correct: ISO_COBOL.md lines 45770, 46001, 46047, 46420, 46487, 46609 all write 'CLASS-ID. <name> INHERITS Base.' with no FROM. A reader working from the markdown general format alone would make FROM mandatory and reject legal source. That is lost content, not lost styling. Nor is dropping underlines a uniform unmarked policy: the transcription carries 225 'Figure notes' blockquotes and 194 explicit 'underlined in the printed standard' statements, so preserving this exact information is the transcription's demonstrated convention — this figure is a hole in it.

One correction to the claim's framing, and one scope enlargement. The claim asserts the omission 'is an oversight, not a transcription policy' because the next figure has a note. That inference overreaches slightly: roughly half of the ~510 fenced figures carry no note, so the absence here is not unique or self-evidently an oversight. More usefully, the gap is a PATTERN, not a one-off: all four 'INHERITS FROM' general formats in the transcription lack a note — line 12539 (class-definition, page 288), 12585 (interface-definition, page 289, this finding), 12817 (11.3.2 CLASS-ID paragraph), 12975 (11.6.2 INTERFACE-ID paragraph). Fixing only page 289 would leave three siblings carrying the same defect, and 11.3.2/11.6.2 are the normative homes of the clause, so they matter more than the overview figures. Severity 'cosmetic' understates it for that reason — the affected fact is 'is FROM required?', which is a syntax-acceptance question a grammar author would get wrong from the markdown alone.
verdict.corrected_description: CONFIRMED with a corrected framing and an enlarged scope. PDF (verified on a ~600 dpi-equivalent magnification of the 300 dpi render): in the page-289 interface-definition general format, IDENTIFICATION, DIVISION, INTERFACE-ID, AS, INHERITS, USING, END and INTERFACE are underlined (required words); FROM carries no underline — the rule stops in the space after 'INHERITS'. Markdown: specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 12581-12592 render the figure as a plain fenced block with no underline marking and no compensating figure note, so the markdown provides no way to know that FROM is an optional word and 'INHERITS interface-name-2' is therefore legal (the standard's own examples at lines 45770/46001/46047/46420/46487/46609 write 'INHERITS Base' with no FROM, independently confirming FROM is optional). This is normative meta-language loss, not formatting: lines 2628/2641/5805 of the transcription state that non-underlined uppercase words are optional words. Two amendments to the original claim: (a) the inference that the missing note 'is an oversight, not a transcription policy' is not established by the adjacent figure alone — about half of the transcription's ~510 fenced figures carry no note, though 194 do carry explicit 'underlined in the printed standard' statements, which is what makes this a hole in a demonstrated convention; (b) the defect is a pattern of four, not one — the same uncompensated 'INHERITS FROM' figure appears at lines 12539 (class-definition, p288), 12585 (interface-definition, p289), 12817 (11.6.2's sibling 11.3.2 CLASS-ID paragraph) and 12975 (11.6.2 INTERFACE-ID paragraph). The fix must add the underline note to all four, and the two paragraph-level formats (12817, 12975) are the normative ones. Severity is better read as minor/semantic than cosmetic, since the lost bit determines whether a conforming compiler must accept 'INHERITS <name>' without FROM.
